decisions.summary: Each arm's first gate call builds its own tool cold (165.9 s / 197.8 s observed), giving up the cross-arm warm cache.

Inside a trial whose purpose is comparing arms' timings, a cache shared across arms is the defect itself. Paying the cold build is what a correct measurement costs. decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-25/27 asks to clean up what the container leaves behind. decisions.summary: The pool-tree exemption from eviction is narrowed: a free tree past the first L7R_BUILDERS (3) trees of its clone's registry, neither held nor the lane's, has its ordinary build profiles taken by the budget step and the low-disk trigger once idle past L7R_CACHE_IDLE_HOURS (12).
decisions.why: Narrows the GM's 2026-11-26 principle ('we definitely don't want to clean things up if it is going to cost us time later') by accepting a contingent later cost the block names itself (a fourth builder's first builder-checks cold, 165.9 s guard / 197.8 s measure). Legitimate on two grounds. (1) Implied by the GM's own 2026-11-27 words that file T515: 'we might have implemented some cleanup that occurs when a builder worktree is cleaned up, but then since we are reusing builder worktrees for efficiency, then maybe that means that a lot of the cleanup that we are relying on never actually happens ... our current tooling is not preventing' - a reused pool tree that is never cleaned is the hole he names. (2) Purpose test: the principle protects caches that save time when used; builder_tree::take hands out the first free tree in registry order, so at the GM's settled count ('start it at 3 builders', 2026-11-26) a handout reaches the fourth tree only when more than three run at once, and eviction needs 12 h of non-use AND a cache past budget or a disk below its free share - so what is taken is a cache the settled loop does not use, and the time it saves at that count is zero. Residual, not a ruling ground: there is no builder cap (T284: 'synchronization rather than pre-emptively limiting builders'), so the 'no handout reaches it' premise rests on take's order plus the 12 h idle test, not on a ceiling; the cold-start price is paid once, and only if the count is raised after an eviction.

That sentence is about a coverage cache that IS used, rarely; this tree's coverage is used only when the tree itself is handed out, which by take's order the settled count does not do, and it is taken not 'just because it's been idle' but only under budget or low-disk pressure after 12 h - the same reach as T526-a, and the same T515 words imply it.
